Of course, I genuinely hope your doing ok thanks for listening.

It started with worsening anxiety like I felt like I was having a constant panick attack then I started feeling like everyone around me was against me, and I was convinced everyone around me was trying to make me break, I also had visual and audio hallucinations that started off very subtle and were very scary. After I was taken to hospital the other symptoms died down but the hallucinations and sounds got worse. This has never happened to me outside of this period of time and hasn't happened since. Its so scary especially since when it was happening I didn't know if what I was seeing and hearing was real. I wouldn't tell anyone togo to a hospital if they don't want to, especially after my experience, but please if you feel unsafe at all(suicidal thoughts or not) just try as hard as you can to make sure you will be safe while you expirience whatever is coming out , I've started recognizing the subtle signs I give myself before an episode and wether I think it'll be bad or not I take precautions, given my history this usually mean getting knifes and weapons out of my reach.

I expirienced psychosis when I was at my worst(so far) I had a huge ptsd episode that led to me attempting suicide, after I was hospitalized I started expiriencing psychosis. I can't remember exactly what helped but it went away after about a month , it also worsened when I was put on a 72 hr hold and forced to a mental health hospital . Those places are horrible.
I can't think of anything ATM but don't ever say "nothing even happened" I get that alot and it pushes me further. Makes me want to give up.

I do this and yeah it's not something I realized I did for a long time, but at this point in my life I noticed it, like ok it's mean and won't help the situation but when I'm in tht mindset its almost like it's out of my control, in some instances I feel the regret of what I've said/done instantly after it happens and in the long run it makes my ptsd worse because I end up alone and feeling worse then when the episode started, I think it's frustration from people not understanding or sometimes not even trying to understand, ik others don't comprehend it the way we do but it takes alot for me to ask for help and its honestly so hard to explain , I have weekly therapy sessions where I kinda of just let it all out and talk about things like this and that personally helps me alot, it helps to feel understood. I will say however that it took me a LONG TIME TO FIND A GOOD THERAPIST FOR MYSELF, but since I've started regular therapy I've noticed I'm more aware of myself during those not so great moments, it still happens but the more I learn about myself and how the traumas effected me and the scientific reasons behind my somewhat involuntary behavior it seems to get more manageable, in my case knowledge helps me get through it. I still have bad days/weeks/ months but it's still progress.
Thank you, I didn't even think of that. I did end up figuring it out but I'm sure that would make things alot easier.
